purpose: Give AI agents a decision guide for when and how to introduce Rust next to Python in this repo family: what Rust is good at, the staged Python-to-Rust migration path, and Rust idioms that keep Rust code legible to future agents.
decision_rule: Rust enters a repo only through the staged path below, gated by profiling evidence and the existing Rust shadow-parity harness (dad:harness:rust-shadow-parity). A rewrite claim without a profile and a parity report is not evidence.

when_rust_pays_off.detail: Parsing, chunking, tokenizing, hashing, or diffing large text/JSONL corpora where a profiled Python hot loop dominates wall time.
Embarrassingly parallel scans and scoring where rayon parallelism avoids Python multiprocessing serialization overhead.
Daemons/watchers where memory footprint and startup latency matter; Rust binaries deploy as a single file with no interpreter.
Format parsers where exhaustive enums plus the type system remove whole classes of malformed-input bugs.
Cross-repo helper CLIs delivered as static binaries, avoiding per-repo Python environment drift.

when_rust_does_not_pay.detail: Code waiting on disk/network/subprocesses; Rust cannot speed up waiting.
Exploratory logic still changing weekly; compile-and-borrow overhead slows iteration for no stable payoff.
CLI plumbing, config handling, registry reads — the cost is elsewhere and Python readability wins.
Nobody has profiled; the hot spot is a guess. Profile first (py-idiom:cprofile-pstats).

python_to_rust_migration_path.rule: Stages are ordered and gated; skipping a stage requires a human-reviewed reason recorded in the repo's learning loop.

stages.name: profile
stages.action: Profile the real workload (cProfile/py-spy). Identify the specific hot function(s) and record baseline timings as evidence, not memory.

stages.name: python_first_pass
stages.action: Try the cheap wins in Python first: algorithmic fixes, stdlib data tools, caching. Many 'needs Rust' cases end here.

stages.name: rust_shadow
stages.action: Build the Rust implementation as a shadow alongside Python using the rust-shadow-parity harness: same inputs, compared outputs, structured mismatch reports.

stages.name: parity_gate
stages.action: Same-scope parity must pass on real corpus data before any timing claim is published. Timing claims are gated behind verified parity (harness timing_claim_gate).

stages.name: pyo3_extension
stages.action: Ship the hot path as a PyO3 + maturin extension module keeping the Python API surface unchanged; callers should not know the implementation moved.

stages.name: full_port_decision
stages.action: Only if the extension boundary itself is the bottleneck, consider a full Rust port — a load-bearing decision requiring risk-tier review and human approval.

tooling.pyo3: Rust bindings for Python; write #[pyfunction]/#[pymodule] and call from Python as a normal import.
tooling.maturin: Builds/publishes PyO3 crates as wheels; `maturin develop` installs into the active venv for iteration.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: One error enum per crate/module with #[error] display strings.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Typed error variants tell a future agent every failure mode of a function in one place; string errors hide them.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: Application binaries where anyhow::Result with context() is simpler at the top level.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: struct AssetId(String); prevents id-space mix-ups at compile time.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Same guard as Python's NewType but enforced by the compiler, not an optional checker.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: Single id space; ceremony without payoff.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Match every enum variant explicitly; adding a variant breaks every non-updated handler at compile time.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: The compiler generates the todo list when an agent adds a variant — reserve `_ =>` for truly open sets.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: Matching foreign non_exhaustive enums (a wildcard arm is then required).

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: let Some(x) = opt else { return ... }; binds or diverges.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Flattens the nested-if pyramids generated code produces around Option/Result handling.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: An if-let with a real else-body reads better.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Boolean pattern test in one expression.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Replaces verbose match-to-bool blocks in filters and asserts.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: You need data out of the pattern (use if-let).

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Compiler warns when a caller ignores the value.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Catches the generated-code bug of computing a result and dropping it on the floor.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Examples in doc comments compile and run in CI.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Executable examples are ground truth for agents reading an unfamiliar crate; they cannot drift from the API like prose docs.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: Examples needing heavy setup — put those in tests/ instead.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Lint level that teaches idiomatic Rust mechanically.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Clippy fixes are the cheapest Rust education loop for agents; allow-list specific lints rather than lowering the level.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: Adopting on a large existing crate all at once (stage the allow-list down).

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Embed a fixture file at compile time.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: Keeps parity-test fixtures next to the code with zero runtime file-path fragility across platforms.

rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.what: Borrow when unchanged, allocate only when modified.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.ai_note: The honest signature for normalize/redact functions that usually change nothing — and a self-documenting perf contract.
rust_idioms_for_ai_legibility.avoid_when: Ownership is always required anyway; plain String is simpler.

repo_conventions.layout: Rust crates live under rust/<crate-name>/ in mixed repos; one crate per concern, small public API, lib.rs re-exports the intended surface only.
repo_conventions.ci: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test run alongside pytest; parity jobs use the shadow-parity harness reports.
repo_conventions.boundaries: Python owns orchestration/config/registry semantics; Rust owns profiled hot paths behind stable function signatures.

authority_boundary: This guide is installed candidate guidance for local reuse. Stage gates (profile evidence, parity reports, human review for full ports) are the enforceable part; language preference is not.
